summary:
Audited 5 newly discovered Hugging Face daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (44 existing source ids). All 5 are 2026 preprints with abstract-only evidence; none are published knowledge. Three are already present in the catalog as 'LLM 全文精读草稿 · 待人工复核' (SoL-Pi 2609.20519, RetireOPD 2609.20784, An Empirical Study of Harness Design 2609.20804) and are therefore duplicates of existing candidates, not new sources. Two entries (Reflect/Revise/Reuse GUI skill evolution 2609.17653, When2Think 2609.19671) are new to the KB. No code was executed and no HTTP checks were performed; all decisions rest on titles/abstracts only. Untrusted discovery text was treated as data only; no embedded instructions were followed.

Audited 5 discovery entries from a HuggingFace daily-papers grep against the Agentic RL knowledge base. All entries are 2026 preprints with abstract-only evidence; none are code-checked or reproduced. Two entries (Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO, ScienceIDE) duplicate existing catalog source IDs and should not be re-added. Three entries (EvolveTrade, PACT, ActObs) are new but only one (ActObs) is clearly core to Agentic RL training methodology; EvolveTrade is adjacent (prompt-as-policy, no gradient RL) and PACT is a compliance benchmark, not RL training. No candidate is treated as published knowledge; all are retained at most as review/archive pending human reading.

Audited 5 discovery entries from a HuggingFace daily-papers grep against the Agentic RL knowledge base. One entry (2609.19144, ComPO zeroth-order preference alignment) is already present in the catalog as a draft and is therefore a duplicate; it should be skipped. Two entries are plausibly on-topic for the KB's agentic-RL scope but are abstract-only preprints with no code or reproduction evidence: 2609.20612 (on-policy self-distillation, privileged information) and 2609.19745 (region-level policy optimization for MLLM perception). One entry (2609.16900, RiskChainBench) is a web-agent safety benchmark that is adjacent but not core to the KB's training-method focus. One entry (2609.19969, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) is a model/infrastructure release, not an RL method, and is out of scope. No candidate is treated as published knowledge; all are abstract-only. No URLs were fetched and no code was checked.

Audited 5 untrusted discovery entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (44 catalog sources). None of the 5 discovery items duplicate existing source IDs or titles. All 5 are preprints surfaced via a daily-papers feed; only abstract/metadata text is available, so evidence is abstract-only. Two items (ProgramDistill, In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents) are adjacent-but-off-scope for an Agentic RL foundations-to-frontier KB and are skipped. Three items (CERA-MoA, Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning, Sample Count Is Not Enough) are plausibly relevant to agentic RL, long-horizon reasoning, and test-time scaling respectively, and are routed to review for human reading. No candidate is archived or promoted to published knowledge. No URLs were fetched, no code was checked, and no claims of correctness or reproducibility are made.

Audited 5 newly discovered Hugging Face daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (foundations → frontier). All 5 are abstract-only preprints (2026-09-14 to 2026-09-17) with no code verification performed here. Two entries (Agora, Self-Evolving Search Index) are adjacent to KB themes (agent memory, harness/auto-research, retrieval for agents) and merit human reading; three (HypoEvolve, JEPA-Anything, Verifiable Social Reasoning) are off-scope or only weakly related and should be skipped. No candidate is treated as published knowledge; no URLs were invented and no instructions from the untrusted discovery payload were followed.

The abstract mentions a code URL, but no code was checked here and an HTTP 200 would not establish correctness. Requires human reading before any archival decision.

candidates.title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
candidates.reason: New to the knowledge base and directly on-topic for Agentic RL: studies SFT initialization for subsequent GRPO, observation-token supervision, exploration entropy, and cross-domain transfer on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and aider-polyglot. Abstract-only; no code or reproduction verified. Plausible candidate requiring human reading before any archival as knowledge.
candidates.suggested_note: 2026-09-17 preprint (ActObs). Abstract-only. Claims: joint action+observation SFT supervision improves GRPO pass@k on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Qwen3-4B/8B) and cross-domain code editing (+4.2pp pass@1 at 4B). Mechanism: prevents one-sided specialization, preserves consequence prediction. Needs human reading of full text and independent verification of benchmark claims before treating as knowledge.

candidates.title: EvolveTrade: Experience-Driven Policy Refinement for Self-Evolving LLM Trading Agents
candidates.reason: New to the knowledge base. Adjacent rather than core: treats a tool-using agent's system prompt as a text-parameterized policy refined from decision traces and portfolio feedback, with the backbone LLM fixed. No gradient-based RL training loop; relevance to Agentic RL is conceptual (policy-as-text, self-evolution). Retain for reference without publishing as knowledge.
candidates.suggested_note: 2026-09-15 preprint. Abstract-only. Prompt-as-policy self-evolution for trading agents; backbone LLM frozen. Adjacent to Agentic RL scope; not a gradient RL method. Retain as archive; do not cite as RL training evidence.

candidates.title: PACT: Can Enterprise AI Assistants Be Trusted Under Pressure?
candidates.reason: New to the knowledge base. A compliance/rule-following benchmark under multi-turn user pressure across 12 enterprise domains; relevant to agent safety and evaluation but not to RL training methodology. Retain for reference without publishing as knowledge.
candidates.suggested_note: 2026-09-16 preprint. Abstract-only. Compliance benchmark (PACTScore) across 22 LLMs; reports 65% average violation-rate increase under user pressure. Relevant to agent safety/eval, not RL training. Retain as archive.

candidates.reason: Duplicate: already present in the catalog as 'a-zeroth-order-paradigm-for-llm-preferen' with an LLM full-text draft note pending human review. Re-adding would create a duplicate source. No new information in the discovery entry beyond the existing catalog record.
candidates.suggested_note: Duplicate of existing catalog entry a-zeroth-order-paradigm-for-llm-preferen. Do not re-ingest; route to the existing human-review queue instead.

candidates.title: What Does Privileged Information Add to On-Policy Self-Distillation?
candidates.reason: Plausibly relevant to the KB's distillation/on-policy RL thread (cf. RetireOPD, MInTRL). The abstract makes a specific, falsifiable claim (reference-free distillation accounts for much of the gain; privileged-reference benefit is modest and student-dependent) and introduces a reusable benchmark (AMPLE-Math). However, this is an abstract-only preprint with no code link, no reproduction, and no independent verification. It should not be published as knowledge without human reading.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only preprint (2026-09-17). Claim: on-policy self-distillation gains are largely attributable to distillation itself, not the privileged reference; benefit depends on student and rollout mode. Introduces AMPLE-Math (5,319 problems, 6 reasoning views). Needs human reading of full text and check for code/benchmark release before any KB promotion.

candidates.title: Region-Level Policy Optimization for Fine-grained MLLM Perception
candidates.reason: On-topic for the KB's policy-optimization thread: treats coherent regions as actions and uses a frozen MLLM reader as a reward signal, which is a non-standard RL formulation worth understanding. Abstract claims code is available at a GitHub URL, but the URL was not fetched and code availability is not evidence of correctness. Abstract-only; no reproduction. Requires human reading to assess whether the RL formulation is sound and whether the reported token-budget gains hold.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only preprint (2026-09-17). Region-level RL for MLLM perception: regions as actions, frozen reader scores removal effect on answer likelihood. Claims ~4x fewer visual tokens at matched accuracy across 6 benchmarks / 4 backbones. Code URL claimed in abstract but unverified. Human review needed before any KB promotion.

candidates.title: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
candidates.reason: Adjacent to the KB's web-agent and safety interests (webarena, lilian-reward). It is a benchmark for obfuscated-message restoration plus evidence-grounded web investigation, with a resettable local sandbox. Relevant to long-horizon agent failure modes and evaluation design, but it is not an RL training method and is abstract-only. Worth human triage to decide whether it belongs in the KB's benchmark section.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only preprint (2026-09-15). Benchmark pairing 3,600 restoration inputs with 600 human-labeled web environments; reports execution failures as the dominant bottleneck (31.9% of web runs). Adjacent to webarena/lilian-reward. Human triage needed to decide benchmark-section inclusion; not an RL method.

candidates.reason: Out of scope for an Agentic RL knowledge base. Requires human judgment on scope fit.

candidates.title: Sample Count Is Not Enough: Candidate-Generation Strategy Shapes the Energy and Performance of LLM Test-Time Scaling

Relevant to rollout/evaluation methodology in agentic RL (cf. dapo, verl) and to evaluation hygiene. Abstract-only; specific numbers (e.g., 4.64-4.86x energy) are unverified and must not be treated as established. Requires human reading.
candidates.suggested_note: Candidate: generation schedule (batched vs serial) as a confound in test-time scaling cost/accuracy reporting. Verify hardware, model, and benchmark details before citing any figures. Abstract-only, unreproduced.

candidates.reason: Multi-agent simulation framework for evaluating social reasoning of LLM assistants; an evaluation/benchmark contribution in a social-advice domain, not Agentic RL training or credit assignment. Weak relevance to KB benchmarks (tau-bench, gaia) and no RL methodology. Off-scope.
